data.description:
Hi everyone,

I recently saw a post about an NYC lobsters meetup, and am wondering how many people here could make it to a London meetup.

If more than a couple of people here are based in London and can make it, I'll organise one in central London.

If you could also let me know which day of the week works best for you, that would be great too!

Cheers!

Shared password manager for families?
data.description:
Long story short, I need to have a bunch of shared accounts with family for finance and insurance and stuff, mostly for the sake of family members who are getting old and need help keeping things organized. So the requirements are:

  • Shared over long distances; just having each of us have our own password manager won't work well
  • Usable for non-techie people, so no command line stuff
  • I can self-host a web thing if necessary
  • Works on Linux and MacOS/iOS

I would just use 1Password, but recent events have demonstrated them as not exactly competent. I could always use KeepassXC and keep the file in a Google Drive folder, or maybe teach my siblings to use Syncthing, but that feels like extra steps we could do without. Anyone have any recommendations for how to do this well?

Rationale for filtering LLM usage links as off-topic
data.description:
Hi, I've been following recent moderation changes and the discussion around them. I understand that the vibecoding tag was conflating multiple meanings and uses, and how moving to the building-LLM-tooling makes it more precise for that subset of the discussion. I also see how people may be tired of the LLM discussion and want to completely filter out anything LLM related.

What I don't quite understand and I'm not sure if it was clearly explained is why stories about "(not) using LLMs" are now considered completely off-topic in this site. There have been plenty of useful discussions around practices and figuring out how to adjust for professional programming in the presence of LLMs over the last few months, and the "flavor" of those discussions is very different from that found in other communities. Also, they seem to still be reasonably encompassed by the current "topicality" guidelines ("Will this improve the reader's next program", etc).

Considering they could still be filtered by anyone not wanting to see anything LLM-related, what is the rationale for not having something like llm-usage as a tag and keep those discussions on the site?
